query: Protocol for establishment and expansion of patient-derived tumor organoids
title: Generation, Expansion, and Biobanking of Gastrointestinal Patient-Derived Organoids from Tumor and Normal Tissues.
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for establishment and expansion of patient-derived tumor organoids

### Overview

This protocol outlines the establishment, expansion, passaging, cryopreservation, and thawing of patient-derived tumor organoids. The process begins with the preparation of specific reagents and media, followed by the processing of primary tissue samples through mechanical and enzymatic dissociation. Organoids are then established in basement membrane extract (BME) within a 24-well plate format. Subsequent sections detail the procedures for passaging confluent cultures, freezing cells for long-term storage using controlled-rate freezing, and thawing frozen aliquots for resumption of culture.

### Materials/Reagents

- Liberase TL (thermolysin low): Stock solution at 13 U/mL; working concentration 0.3 U/mL in PBS.
- DNAse I solution: 30 mg/mL diluted in sterile H2O.
- ROCK inhibitor (RocKi) Y-27632: 10 mM in DMSO.
- Basal Medium (BM): DMEM/F12 supplemented with HEPES 10 mM, L-glutamine 2 mM, Penicillin/Streptomycin (P/S) 1.5X, Normocin 150 μg/mL, N2 supplement 1X, and NeuroCultTM SM1 1X. Filtered through a 0.22 μm Stericup vacuum filtration system.
- Colon Tumor Medium (CTM): BM supplemented with N-acetyl-L-cysteine 1 mM, nicotinamide 10 mM, EGF 50 ng/mL, Noggin 100 ng/mL, A-8301 0.5 μM, SB202190 10 μM, gastrin 10 nM, R-Spondin1 500 ng/mL, FGF10 10 ng/mL, PGE2 10 nM, and RocKi Y-27632 10 μM.
- Basement Membrane Extract (BME): Thawed and kept on ice.
- Trypan blue.
- Bambanker freezing medium.
- Trypsin Express.
- PBS (cold and tempered to 37 °C).
- Sterile H2O.

### Equipment

- CO2 incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2).
- Culture hood with UV light.
- Centrifuge (capable of cooling to 4 °C).
- Ice bucket.
- 50-mL Falcon tubes.
- 60 mm Petri dishes.
- Sterile tips and serological pipettes with filters (15 mL and 50 mL).
- 15 mL Falcon tubes.
- Scalpels.
- Cryotubes.
- 70 μm cell strainer.
- Neubauer chamber.
- 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
- 24-well plates.
- P1000 pipette tips.
- CoolCell device (-1 °C/min rate).
- -80 °C freezer.
- Liquid N2 tank.

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain strict aseptic technique throughout all steps. Clean the culture hood and leave the UV light on for 15 minutes prior to starting. Use sterile plastic materials including Petri dishes, tips, pipettes, and tubes. Handle biological samples carefully to avoid contamination. Ensure proper disposal of biohazardous waste.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Prepare the stock solution of Liberase TL (thermolysin low) at 13 U/mL. Dilute this stock to achieve a working concentration of 0.3 U/mL in PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare a DNAse I solution at a concentration of 30 mg/mL diluted in sterile H2O. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare ROCK inhibitor (RocKi) Y-27632 as a 10 mM solution in DMSO. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare Basal Medium (BM) consisting of DMEM/F12, HEPES 10 mM, L-glutamine 2 mM, P/S 1.5X, Normocin 150 μg/mL, N2 supplement 1X, and NeuroCultTM SM1 1X. Filter the media through a 0.22 μm Stericup vacuum filtration system. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Prepare Colon Tumor Medium (CTM) by supplementing Basal Medium with N-acetyl-L-cysteine 1 mM, nicotinamide 10 mM, EGF 50 ng/mL, Noggin 100 ng/mL, A-8301 0.5 μM, SB202190 10 μM, gastrin 10 nM, R-Spondin1 500 ng/mL, FGF10 10 ng/mL, PGE2 10 nM, and RocKi Y-27632 10 μM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Thaw the Basement Membrane Extract (BME) and keep it on ice until use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->

## Primary Tissue Processing

### Start

1. Preheat a 24-well plate in the CO2 incubator at 37 °C. Prepare a 50-mL Falcon tube containing 10 mL of cold PBS plus 2X antibiotics to receive the tissue sample. Clean the culture hood and place all necessary plastic materials inside, including 60 mm Petri dishes, sterile tips, serological pipettes with filters (15 mL and 50 mL), 15 mL and 50-mL Falcon tubes, scalpels, and cryotubes. Turn on the UV light for 15 minutes. Cool the centrifuge to 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Collect the tissue sample into the prepared PBS Falcon tube and place the tube in an ice bucket. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Outside the hood, decant the PBS into a sterile Falcon tube, being careful not to discard the sample. Perform 6-7 washes with cold PBS, using approximately 10 mL per wash. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. Transfer the sample to a new Falcon tube containing PBS plus 2X antibiotics and incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
5. Wash the sample three times with sterile PBS without antibiotics, allowing 5 minutes for each wash. In the final wash, retain approximately 1 mL of PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
6. Transfer the tissue fragments into a 60 mm Petri dish containing the remaining 1 mL of PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
7. Cut or crush the tissue fragments into very small pieces using a scalpel and recover all fragments into a 15 mL Falcon tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
8. Digest the tissue with Liberase at a final concentration of 0.3 U/mL. Add 23 μL of the 13 U/mL Liberase stock solution for each mL of sample volume. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->
9. Incubate the digestion mixture for 45-60 minutes at 37 °C in a water bath. Inside the hood, pipette the mixture gently with a P1000 tip every 15 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S09 -->
10. After mechanical and enzymatic dissociation, filter the tube contents through a 70 μm cell strainer into a new 50-mL Falcon tube. Rinse the strainer with 1 mL of PBS to recover released tissue cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S10 -->
11. Centrifuge the filtered suspension at 500× g for 5 minutes at 4 °C. Carefully discard the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S11 -->
12. Resuspend the final cell pellet in 500 μL of cold Basal Medium (BM). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S12 -->
13. Count the number of cells with Neubauer chamber taking 5 μL of tube content and adding 45 μL of trypan blue (see Note 18). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S13 -->

## Organoid Establishment

### Plating

1. Plate cells at a density between 200,000 and 300,000 cells in 50 μL of 50% BME (diluted in BM) per well of 24-well plate (see Notes 19 and 20). To do that, calculate the volume of cells according to the number of wells that will be plated. Transfer this volume to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
2. Centrifuge the Eppendorf tube at 500× g for 5 minutes at 4 °C. Carefully remove the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
3. Calculate the total volume of 50% BME required by multiplying the number of wells by 50 μL per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
4. Remove the preheated 24-well plate from the incubator just before plating, ensuring it remains at 37 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
5. Resuspend the cell pellet in the calculated volume of cold BM. Add an equal volume of 100% BME to create a 50% BME solution. Quickly plate 50 μL of this mixture into each well of the tempered 24-well plate, forming a dome without introducing bubbles. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
6. Incubate the plate for 20-30 minutes at 37 °C with 5% CO2 to allow the BME to solidify. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->
7. Once the BME has solidiﬁed, add 500 μL of appropriate 37 °C- tempered medium in each well. Add medium ST for normal colon organoids and gastric organoids. Add selective CTM medium for tumor colon organoids. In all cases RocKi Y-27632 must be added (see Note 23). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S07 -->
8. Place the plates in the cell culture incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S08 -->
9. Refresh the medium every 2-3 days. Remove old medium by tilting the plate and placing the pipette tip near the edge, avoiding contact with the BME dome. Add 500 μL of fresh, 37 °C-tempered medium. Include RocKi Y-27632 only during the first medium change; omit it in subsequent changes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S09 -->

## Passaging

### High Confluence

> **Operational constraint:** When organoid cultures reach high confluence within the dome, split and expand them to additional wells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
1. Remove the medium from each well using a pipette. Wash the wells with PBS tempered to 37 °C and remove the PBS with the pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
2. Add 1 mL of cold PBS to disrupt the BME dome mechanically. Centrifuge at 500× g for 5 minutes at 4 °C and discard the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
3. Add 250 μL of Trypsin Express to the organoid sediment. Resuspend by pipetting and incubate in a 37 °C water bath for no more than 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->
4. Add 2 mL of cold Basal Medium (BM) to stop the digestion and mix well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S05 -->
5. Centrifuge at 500× g for 5 minutes at 4 °C. Remove the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S06 -->
6. Proceed with steps 3 through 9 of the organoid establishment protocol to replate the cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S07 -->

## Cryopreservation

### Freezing

1. Follow steps 2 through 6 of the organoid passaging procedure to prepare the cell suspension. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
2. Add 1 mL of Bambanker freezing medium to each cryotube intended for freezing. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->
3. Resuspend the cell sediment in the freezing medium and transfer 1 mL into each cryovial. Place the cryotubes in a CoolCell device for controlled-rate freezing at -1 °C/min for 24 hours in a -80 °C freezer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S03 -->

### After that time

1. After 24 hours in the -80 °C freezer, transfer the cryotubes to a liquid nitrogen tank for long-term storage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S01 -->

## Thawing

### Thawing

1. To thaw a cryotube, prepare a 15 mL Falcon tube containing 5 mL of cold Basal Medium (BM) and defrost an aliquot of BME on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. Preheat a 24-well plate in the incubator at 37 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->
3. Quickly thaw the cryotube and transfer its contents into the 15 mL Falcon tube containing 5 mL of cold BM. Mix by inversion. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S03 -->
4. Centrifuge the suspension at 500× g for 5 minutes at 4 °C. Remove the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S04 -->
5. Proceed with steps 3 through 9 of the organoid establishment protocol to replate the cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S05 -->

## References

- [1] Generation, Expansion, and Biobanking of Gastrointestinal Patient-Derived Organoids from Tumor and Normal Tissues. — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38478340/
